title: CT Case Record
description: One CT study (or one screenshot of a study) described in structured form.

added.description: Date this record entered the base (YYYY-MM-DD).

patient.description: Pseudonymous patient context. Never store real identifiers.

id.description: Pseudonym linking studies of the same patient, e.g. PT-A.

clinical_context.description: Indication, known history, relevant labs — whatever was supplied.

frames.description: The screenshots this record was read from. One acquisition can supply many frames at different levels and windows — they all belong to this one case, never to separate cases.

id.description: Short slug unique within the case, e.g. 'carina-soft-tissue'.

slice_level.description: Anatomic level of this frame, e.g. 'carina', 'L2 vertebral body'.

read_after_report.description: True if this frame was supplied after the official report was known. Such a frame documents what the reported findings look like; it cannot test the screenshot read, and findings first seen on it must not be scored as concordant.

annotations.description: Marked regions on this frame. Coordinates are fractions of image width/height (0-1), so they survive rescaling.

label.description: Short text drawn beside the marker.

r.description: Marker radius as a fraction of image width. Defaults to 0.05.

kind.description: 'confirmed' = this is the thing. 'candidate' = one of several possibilities, drawn dashed. 'search_zone' = look here, no claim about what is there.

findings.description: Discrete observations. An empty array means an unremarkable read.

impression.description: Plain-language synthesis of what the frame shows.

confidence.description: How much weight this read can carry given image quality and context.

limitations.description: What this record cannot establish — single frame, no priors, unknown window, etc.

official_report.description: The reporting radiologist's findings, where supplied. This is ground truth for the case and outranks the screenshot-derived read everywhere they disagree.

text.description: The report findings as supplied, verbatim.

provided_by.description: Where it came from, e.g. 'user-supplied official report'.

read_delta.description: Honest account of where the screenshot read agreed with, misattributed, or missed what the report describes.

compare_to.description: Case IDs this study has been formally compared against.

id.description: Short slug stable across studies of the same patient, e.g. 'liver-seg7-lesion'. This is what comparison matches on.

organ.description: Anatomic structure: liver, lung, kidney, aorta, vertebra, ...

location.description: Segment / lobe / level, e.g. 'segment VII', 'RLL posterior basal'.

description.description: What is actually seen, in descriptive terms.

size_mm.description: Measured axes in mm, longest first. 1-3 values.

attenuation_hu.description: Density in Hounsfield units, where readable.

morphology.description: Descriptors: cystic, solid, ground_glass, cavitary, calcified, necrotic, ...

significance.description: Weight of the finding. 'critical' = would need urgent attention if real.

seen_on.description: Frame ids this finding was actually visible on. Absence from a frame that does not cut through the finding means nothing.

source.description: Where this finding came from. Findings sourced from the official report may describe things no supplied frame shows.

concordance.description: How the screenshot read fared against the official report. 'recharacterised' means the feature was seen but attributed wrongly; 'missed' means it was not identified at all; 'over_called' means the screenshot read asserted something the report does not support.
